manual/Animation.html.title: Transition animation | UITK Navigation
manual/Animation.html.summary: Transition animation NavElement has independent Show and Hide transitions. Each transition can combine Move, Rotate, Scale, and Fade channels, driven by LitMotion on a real-time scheduler by default. Popups use the same transition system but configure their Backdrop and Content as separate layers. Start with a preset In the UI Builder Inspector: Select the NavElement and open Transitions. Choose the Show or Hide tab. Select a Preset category and Variant. Click Apply. Open the Move, Rotate, Scale, and Fade cards to tune the copied values. Use the Play icon to preview the selected tab and Reset to restore the element's On Start state. Apply bakes the chosen preset into the current channel values. After the preset block loses focus, its category returns to None while the copied channel configuration remains. This makes a preset a starting point rather than a locked style. In hand-authored raw UXML, preset-category and the one-based preset-variant can also remain as runtime settings. Any manually enabled channel overrides the corresponding channel built by that preset. An out-of-range Variant is ignored. Built-in preset library The package contains 21 categories and 351 variants. Every variant includes separate Show and Hide definitions. Category Variants Category Variants Back 8 Basic1 25 Basic2 25 Bounce 15 Default 1 Discrete 20 Drift 10 Drop 15 Fade 25 Flip 10 Ghost 10 Gradual 12 Jelly 10 Organic1 25 Organic2 25 Rotate 25 Shake 10 Slide1 25 Slide2 25 Spin 10 Zoom 20 Choose None when you want to build the transition entirely from manual channels. Preset variant numbers start at 1. Animation channels Channel UI Toolkit style Main values Move translate From/To reference, direction or custom pixel position, offset Rotate rotate From/To Z-axis angle and offset Scale scale From/To Vector2 scale and offset Fade opacity From/To opacity and offset Move provides edge and anchor directions such as Left, Top, BottomRight, and MiddleCenter, plus Custom Position. Direction distances are calculated from the parent content rectangle and the transformed bounds of the element. Note UI Toolkit rotation is 2D. Only the Z axis is applied; Y-axis rotation from a source preset is not available. Reference values Each From and To side chooses a reference: Reference Meaning Start Value The channel's captured rest/start value Current Value The resolved style when the transition is prepared Custom Value An explicitly entered value Offset is added to the resolved reference. Keep the final resting layout in UXML or USS: transform styles applied by the animator are cleared after completion. Timing and playback Every enabled channel has its own settings: Setting Behavior Delay Wait before this channel begins; must be zero or greater Duration Length of one cycle; default 0.3 seconds Ease LitMotion Ease value, or a custom Animation Curve Play Mode Normal, Ping Pong, Spring, or Shake Loops Additional cycles: 0 plays once, 1 plays twice, -1 repeats forever All enabled channels run in parallel. The longest finite channel determines when Show or Hide finishes. Infinite loops are forced to Ping Pong and never report completion. Caution Do not use Loops = -1 on a transition whose lifecycle must finish. Infinite Show prevents ShowFinished and Auto Hide; infinite Hide prevents the View from closing and can leave a popup Completion task pending. The default scheduler is MotionScheduler.UpdateRealtime. Animations and graph Time Delay outputs therefore continue while Time.timeScale is 0. Interruption and reversal UIViewVisibility tracks NotVisible, Showing, Visible, and Hiding, plus continuous progress. When Hide is requested during Show, or Show during Hide, the opposite transition starts at mirrored progress instead of restarting from its beginning. This keeps rapid navigation responsive. While LitMotion is active, the animator temporarily suppresses the element's USS transition-duration and restores it afterward, preventing two animation systems from fighting over the same styles. Hide mode When Hidden Result Display Applies display: none; removes the View from layout Visibility Keeps display: flex and applies visibility: hidden; preserves layout Both modes ignore picking while hidden. Move, Rotate, and Scale automatically request UsageHints.DynamicTransform; Fade requests UsageHints.DynamicColor. Animation ownership in 0.3.1 UIViewVisibility owns its Show and Hide UIAnimation settings directly. The legacy UIAnimationPreset ScriptableObject and UIViewVisibility.Preset property were removed in 0.3.1. Configure reusable Category/Variant values through UXML templates or copy the animation settings in Editor tooling.

manual/GettingStart.html.title: Getting started | UITK Navigation
manual/GettingStart.html.summary: Getting started This walkthrough builds Home → Settings and then routes Settings back through a shared Home destination. 1. Author the UXML Create two NavElement roots and place a NavButton inside Home. <ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements" xmlns:nav="NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Elements"> <nav:NavElement name="home" view-category="Demo" view-key="Home"> <nav:NavButton text="Settings" signal-category="Demo" signal-key="OpenSettings" /> </nav:NavElement> <nav:NavElement name="settings" view-category="Demo" view-key="Settings" /> </ui:UXML> 2. Register addresses Open Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog and add: Tab Address View Demo / Home View Demo / Settings Signal Demo / OpenSettings Assign these addresses in UI Builder and save the UXML. 3. Build the graph Create and open a UI Navigation Graph. Configure Home to Show Demo/Home and Hide Demo/Settings on enter. Add a Database Signal output Demo/OpenSettings and connect it to Settings. Configure Settings to Show Demo/Settings and Hide Demo/Home. Add a Custom Signal output Home on Settings. Create Send Signal, set Address Type = Custom and Custom Signal = Home, then connect the Settings output to its Multi Enter. Create a Portal with Type = Signal, Signal Address = Custom, Custom Signal = Home, and connect its output to Home. Save the graph. The Settings output does not need a special Destinations port. Its existing Signal output connects directly to Send Signal. 4. Connect the runtime Add one enabled UINavigatorBehaviour, assign the graph, and ensure the UXML is attached to a Player-context panel. Optionally add UIBackInputRouter for Escape, Backspace, and mouse Back/Forward. In Play Mode, NavButton opens Settings. Sending Custom Home reaches Send Signal, resolves the matching Portal, and enters Home. Application code can request the same route with Signal.Send("Home").

manual/KeyCatalog.html.title: Key Catalog | UITK Navigation
manual/KeyCatalog.html.summary: Key Catalog Open Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog to manage Database addresses shared by UXML, graphs, and code. The catalog is an Editor authoring registry; runtime matching uses serialized values. Catalogs Tab Used by View NavElement, UI Show/Hide commands, and UI View outputs Toggle NavToggle, Toggle outputs, and Toggle Portal conditions Signal NavButton, Signal.Send(UIKey), Signal outputs, Send Signal, and Signal Portals Every Database address is a case-sensitive Category / Key pair. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed. Custom Signals are graph-local strings and are intentionally not registered in the catalog. Workflow Add a Category and Key in the correct tab. Assign it from a UI Builder or Graph Inspector picker. Use Scan Project to discover addresses in UXML and .uinavgraph assets. Use Refresh Usage to update reference counts without modifying the catalog. Scanning does not parse arbitrary C# strings. Register code-only Database addresses manually. Rename previews and updates supported UXML and graph references together; deleting only removes the catalog entry and leaves serialized usages intact. The catalog is stored at ProjectSettings/UITKNavigationKeyCatalog.asset. Commit it with the assets that use it. It is not included in player builds.

manual/NavigationGraph.html.title: Navigation Graph | UITK Navigation
manual/NavigationGraph.html.summary: Navigation Graph A Navigation Graph separates screen flow from the UXML hierarchy. Unity Graph Toolkit stores the editable .uinavgraph; saving validates it and imports a runtime UINavigationAsset used by UINavigatorBehaviour. Asset lifecycle Create Assets > Create > UI Navigation > UI Navigation Graph. Edit nodes, inspector options, and connections. Save the graph to validate and rebuild its runtime asset. Assign the graph to the single active UINavigatorBehaviour. Editor tools and generators can also use code-first authoring. Nodes Node Purpose Start Declares the single initial route UI Applies View commands and exposes Signal, Toggle, Delay, and View outputs Send Signal Collects UI outputs and resolves a matching Signal Portal without rendering Portal Defines the global destination route for a Signal or Toggle Random Chooses one branch by relative Weight Time Scale Sets Time.timeScale and continues an Action chain Debug Log Writes a Console message Load Scene Starts a Single or Additive scene load Set Active Loaded Scene Makes a loaded scene active Unload Scene Unloads a scene while protecting the last loaded scene Application Quit Quits a build or stops Editor Play Mode The Pivot node was removed in 0.4.0. See its migration page. Routes and history UI outputs normally connect directly to a UI or Action chain. Multiple outputs that should reach one global destination connect to the Multi input of Send Signal; the matching Portal owns the route to the actual UI. Portal matching is global and runs before outputs on the active UI node. Push records the previous screen, Replace changes screens without modifying history, and Back executes connected Actions before requesting history navigation. Enable Clear History when entering a UI or Send Signal destination should discard both Back and Forward stacks. Enable Use Back on a UI node that may consume a graph Back request. Follow Play Mode Enable Tools > UI Navigation > Follow Play Mode In Graph to highlight the active runtime node while testing.

manual/Popup.html.title: Popups | UITK Navigation
manual/Popup.html.summary: Popups Popups use a panel-local LIFO stack that is independent of the Navigation Graph. Each call clones a VisualTreeAsset, optionally assigns a data source, animates it into the panel, and returns an awaitable result. Set up a host Add UIPopupHost to the GameObject that owns the panel's PanelRenderer. The host requires that component and creates its popup layer when PanelRenderer supplies a UI root. public sealed class PopupExample : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private UIPopupHost popupHost; [SerializeField] private VisualTreeAsset messagePopup; } Call Show only after the panel root has been initialized. Calling it before the UI root is ready throws an InvalidOperationException. Build a popup template Every popup VisualTreeAsset must contain: exactly one UIPopupView; exactly one UIPopupContent inside that View; zero or one UIPopupBackdrop inside that View. Invalid counts throw an exception that includes the number found. The failed instance is rolled back and is not left on the stack. <ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements" xmlns:popup="NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Popup"> <popup:UIPopupView close-on-backdrop="false" back-behavior="Close"> <popup:UIPopupBackdrop /> <popup:UIPopupContent> <ui:Label> <Bindings> <ui:DataBinding property="text" data-source-path="Title" binding-mode="ToTarget" /> </Bindings> </ui:Label> <ui:VisualElement name="dynamic-content" /> <popup:UIPopupActionButton text="Cancel" action-id="cancel" close-popup="true" /> <popup:UIPopupActionButton text="OK" action-id="confirm" close-popup="true" /> </popup:UIPopupContent> </popup:UIPopupView> </ui:UXML> The package supplies full-panel positioning and these USS classes: ui-popup-view, ui-popup-backdrop, ui-popup-content, and ui-popup-action-button. Your template USS is responsible for Backdrop color, Content placement and size, spacing, and typography. Show and await a popup Use ShowAsync when only the final result matters: UIPopupResult result = await popupHost.ShowAsync( messagePopup, new MessagePopupModel { Title = "Notice" }, configure: view => view.Q("dynamic-content")?.Add(new Label("Runtime content")), cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Debug.Log($"Action={result.ActionId}, Reason={result.Reason}"); Annotate model properties used by UI Toolkit data binding with [CreateProperty] from Unity.Properties. The model becomes the UIPopupView.dataSource before Show. Use Show when you also need the handle: UIPopupHandle handle = popupHost.Show(messagePopup, model); handle.ActionInvoked += actionId => Debug.Log($"Invoked: {actionId}"); UIPopupResult result = await handle.Completion; UIPopupHandle.IsOpen remains true until the Hide transition finishes. Call handle.Close() for that specific instance, popupHost.CloseTop() for the top item, or popupHost.CloseAll() for the entire host. Actions and results UIPopupActionButton trims and raises its action-id. With close-popup="true", it closes the popup and returns that ID. With false, it raises ActionInvoked but leaves Completion pending until something else closes the popup. Close reason Produced by Action An action button that closes the popup Back Back behavior Close Backdrop A direct Backdrop click with close-on-backdrop="true" Programmatic Close, CloseTop, or CloseAll HostDetached Host disable, panel root reload, or detach Cancellation is different from a close result. A canceled token removes the instance immediately and completes the task as canceled. If the token is already canceled, the template is not instantiated. Stack, Back, and focus The last popup shown is the first one closed. Only the topmost, non-closing popup receives the high-priority Back policy: Back behavior Result Close Closes the top popup and consumes Back Block Keeps the popup open and consumes Back PassThrough Keeps it open and lets Back continue to the graph or a lower handler When shown, the popup focuses its first enabled focusable descendant. When the top popup closes, focus returns to the previously focused element; if that element no longer exists, focus moves to the popup below. close-on-backdrop reacts only when the Backdrop itself is the click target. Clicking a child placed inside the Backdrop does not count as a direct Backdrop click. Popup transitions UIPopupView provides separate Backdrop Transitions and Content Transitions, each with independent Show/Hide presets and channels. Both layers play together and the longer finite layer determines completion. Closing does not complete the handle until Hide finishes. Avoid infinite Hide loops, because the popup cannot finalize while its Hide transition never completes. See Transition animation for preset, timing, reversal, and Loop details.

manual/Signals.html.title: Signals | UITK Navigation
manual/Signals.html.summary: Signals UITK Navigation 0.4.0 uses one Signal channel for NavButton, application code, UI node outputs, Send Signal, and Signal Portals. Address types Address Type Value Use it for Database Category / Key from the Signal catalog Shared, project-wide addresses and code using UIKey Custom One graph-local string such as Home, Back, or Close Short routes that do not need a catalog entry Custom matching is case-sensitive and uses ordinal comparison. Home and home are different. Avoid interpolation, concatenation, case conversion, and ToString() in a frequently executed dispatch path; reuse an existing string or constant. Send from code using NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Identity; using NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Navigation; bool databaseByParts = Signal.Send("Menu", "OpenSettings"); bool databaseByKey = Signal.Send(new UIKey("Menu", "OpenSettings")); bool custom = Signal.Send("Home"); Every overload returns true when the active navigator handled or queued the request. It returns false for an empty/invalid address, when no active navigator exists, or when no route handles the Signal. The service checks a matching Portal before the active UI node. A Custom Signal can match a Custom Signal output or Portal; it is not automatically converted into a Database address. Note Toggle remains a separate channel and uses the Toggle catalog. NavToggle does not call Signal.Send.

manual/Troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | UITK Navigation
manual/Troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting Start with the first Console error. A Navigation Graph that fails to import cannot update its compiled runtime asset, so later runtime symptoms may be consequences of that authoring error. Package compilation ZLinq.dll or the ZLinq namespace is missing ZLinq.Unity is an adapter and does not contain the core library. Install the ZLinq NuGet package with NuGetForUnity first, then install the ZLinq.Unity UPM package. See Installation. If both are installed, verify that their versions are compatible and that the NuGet package produced the core assembly under Assets/Packages. LitMotion types are missing Install LitMotion 2.0.0 or newer with the Git URL in Installation. Allow Unity to finish importing LitMotion before installing or reimporting UITK Navigation. Graph authoring The Navigation Graph creation or editor menu is missing Verify that the project uses Unity 6000.6.0b5 or newer. Confirm that com.unity.graphtoolkit 0.5.0-exp.1 is resolved in Package Manager. Resolve the earliest Graph Toolkit or UITK Navigation compile error in the Console. Reimport the .uinavgraph after compilation succeeds. UITK Navigation uses Graph Toolkit for authoring and compiles the graph to a runtime UINavigationAsset; a Graph Toolkit error therefore blocks graph import. See Requirements. The graph reports validation errors Check these structural rules: The graph contains at least one Screen node and exactly one Start node. Start connects to exactly one Screen Enter. Every Screen has a non-empty, unique Node ID. A UI output connects to exactly one UI, Action, or Send Signal target; Send Signal accepts multiple incoming UI outputs. UI outputs do not duplicate the same trigger and address on one node. Random has at least one connected output, non-negative finite weights, and a connected weight sum greater than zero. Each Send Signal has a non-empty Database or Custom address, at least one Enter connection, and a matching Signal Portal. Each Portal has a valid address, a unique condition, and exactly one target. Time Scale and Scene Action values satisfy the constraints described by their node pages. Warnings for unregistered addresses do not always stop compilation, but they usually indicate that UXML and graph values no longer agree. Navigation at runtime Play Mode starts with a blank UI Make sure exactly one enabled UINavigatorBehaviour exists. A duplicate disables itself and logs an error. Assign the intended .uinavgraph to its Navigation Graph field. Verify that Start reaches the expected first UI node. Add the first View address to that UI node's On Enter > Show list. Confirm that a matching NavElement is attached to a live Player-context panel. Compare Category and Key exactly, including case. UINavigatorBehaviour waits briefly for Views to register, then initializes the graph. A View that never attaches to a panel cannot receive the initial Show command. A button, toggle, or signal does not navigate Match the sender, address type, and graph trigger: Sender Catalog tab Graph route NavButton Signal Database Signal output or Signal Portal Signal.Send(UIKey) Signal Database Signal output or Signal Portal Signal.Send(string) None Custom Signal output or Custom Signal Portal NavToggle Toggle Toggle output or Toggle Portal with the expected On/Off value Then verify the exact value and Address Type. Database Default / Home and Custom Home are different addresses. Custom matching is case-sensitive. Normal UI outputs are evaluated only on the active UI node; Portals are global and are tested first. Send Signal does not reach its destination Connect at least one existing UI output directly to Send Signal's Multi Enter. Assign a non-empty Database or Custom address in Go To. Create a Signal Portal with the same Address Type and exact value. Connect the Portal output to one UI or Action chain. Send Signal has no output by design. The matching Portal owns the downstream route. More than one View animates at once This is expected when multiple attached NavElement instances share the same View address. The registry broadcasts Show and Hide commands to every matching instance. Give each independently controlled View a unique Category / Key. A UI View route occurs earlier than expected UI View outputs fire when a matching Animated Show or Hide transition starts, not when its animation completes. Instant View commands and InstantShow() or InstantHide() do not fire this output. Use a Time Delay, a different application signal, or another graph step when routing must wait. Transitions A View changes visibility but does not move Confirm that the Move channel is enabled or that a preset containing Move was applied. Ensure the animated element receives a non-zero resolved width and height from layout. If the View starts with display: none, UITK Navigation performs a layout warm-up for up to four frames before starting a Move animation. In UI Builder, selecting a preset applies its values to the Show/Hide channels and then resets the preset selector to None. Inspect the channel values rather than expecting the selector to remain selected. See Transition animation for channel precedence, timing, and Hide Mode. A transition, popup result, or async operation never completes Check every active animation channel for Loops = -1. Infinite channels repeat in Ping Pong mode and never report completion, so a visibility transition or Popup close that awaits them cannot settle. Use a finite loop count for lifecycle transitions. Animations continue while Time.timeScale is zero This is intentional by default. Navigation delays use unscaled time and transition animation starts with a real-time scheduler, so menus and Popups continue to work while gameplay is paused unless you replace the View scheduler. Back navigation Escape or the mouse Back button does nothing Add and enable UIBackInputRouter. It translates Escape, Backspace, and mouse Back/Forward buttons into navigation requests through the Input System. For graph history to handle Back, the active Screen must enable Use Back and history must contain a previous Screen. A visible View with Hide On Back or Block Back has priority. The topmost Popup has still higher priority: Close closes it, Block consumes Back, and PassThrough lets navigation below it continue. Popups UIPopupHost says the UI root is not ready Place UIPopupHost on the same GameObject as PanelRenderer, enable the renderer, and call Show only after the panel root has initialized. See Popups. A popup template is rejected The template must contain exactly one UIPopupView, exactly one UIPopupContent inside it, and zero or one UIPopupBackdrop. Remove duplicate wrappers and do not place the required Content outside the View. Clicking an action does not complete ShowAsync UIPopupActionButton with close-popup="false" raises its action but deliberately keeps the Popup open. Close its handle, call CloseTop, or set close-popup="true" when that action should complete the task. Scene Action nodes A scene does not load, activate, or unload Add named or indexed scenes to Build Settings and verify the selected reference mode. Set Active Loaded Scene and Unload Scene require the scene to be loaded already. The last loaded scene cannot be unloaded. If Allow Scene Activation is disabled on Load Scene, call UINavigatorBehaviour.ActivatePendingScene() when activation should continue. An Action node's Next chain continues immediately after the request is issued; it does not wait for Unity's asynchronous scene operation to finish. Trigger post-load UI from the destination scene or an explicit completion signal when ordering matters. The Key picker does not show an address Open Key Catalog, select the correct View/Toggle/Signal tab, and run Scan Project. Add code-only Database addresses manually. Custom Signals do not appear in Key Catalog.

manual/UxmlElements.html.title: UXML elements | UITK Navigation
manual/UxmlElements.html.summary: UXML elements This section covers the three UI Builder controls that connect a visual tree to the Key Catalog and Navigation Graph. Popup-specific UXML controls are covered in Popups. Element Base control Catalog Purpose NavElement VisualElement View Registers a graph-controlled View and owns Show/Hide transitions NavButton Button Signal Publishes a Database Signal address when clicked NavToggle Toggle Button Publishes a Toggle address and its bool value Namespace Add the package namespace to hand-authored UXML: <ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements" xmlns:nav="NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Elements"> <nav:NavElement name="main" view-category="Menu" view-key="Main"> <nav:NavButton text="Settings" signal-category="Menu" signal-key="OpenSettings" /> <nav:NavToggle label="Music" toggle-category="Settings" toggle-key="Music" /> </nav:NavElement> </ui:UXML> UI Builder writes the same attributes when you select addresses from its catalog pickers. Register entries in Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog first so the correct View or Button picker can find them. Address contract An address is the case-sensitive Category/Key pair represented by UIKey. The same address must be used at both ends: UXML side Graph side NavElement View address On Enter/Exit Show or Hide, or UI View output (Animated start only) NavButton Signal address (signal-* attributes) Database Signal output or Signal Portal NavToggle Toggle address Toggle output or Toggle Portal NavButton uses the Signal catalog and the same Signal channel as Signal.Send(UIKey). At runtime, a valid NavElement registers when it attaches to a Player-context panel. Graph View commands find that registry entry and call its animated or instant visibility methods. UI Builder previews do not register runtime Views.

manual/index.html.title: UITK Navigation | UITK Navigation
manual/index.html.summary: UITK Navigation UITK Navigation is a screen-flow package for Unity UI Toolkit. Author navigation with Graph Toolkit, animate NavElement visibility with LitMotion, and display panel-local LIFO popups. Features Compiles .uinavgraph sources into runtime UINavigationAsset assets on save. Routes Database or Custom Signals through render-free Send Signal destinations and Portals. Provides NavElement, NavButton, and NavToggle for UI Builder and UXML. Combines Move, Rotate, Scale, and Fade channels into Show/Hide transitions. Supports Back/Forward history, delays, Toggle branches, and scene or application actions. Searches and renames project-wide UI addresses through the Key Catalog. Displays popups with async results and focus restoration through UIPopupHost or UIPopupStack. Start with Requirements, Installation, and Getting started. Note This documentation targets Unity 6000.6.0b5. Unity 6.6 is the recommended baseline.

manual/installation.html.title: Installation | UITK Navigation
manual/installation.html.summary: Installation A clean installation takes only a few minutes. Install the dependencies first, then add UITK Navigation. Important ZLinq has a NuGet core package and a separate Unity package. Follow the order below so Unity can compile each assembly as it arrives. 1. Install NuGetForUnity and core ZLinq Install NuGetForUnity by following its Unity installation instructions. In Unity, open Window > NuGet > Manage NuGet Packages. Search for ZLinq, select the package, and click Install. Confirm that a ZLinq package folder is present under Assets/Packages. This installs the core assembly. The Unity integration is added in the next step. 2. Install the Git dependencies Open Window > Package Manager, click +, and choose Install package from git URL.... Enter and install each URL separately, in this order: https://github.com/annulusgames/LitMotion.git?path=src/LitMotion/Assets/LitMotion https://github.com/Cysharp/ZLinq.git?path=src/ZLinq.Unity/Assets/ZLinq.Unity These packages are maintained at annulusgames/LitMotion and Cysharp/ZLinq. 3. Install UITK Navigation Use Install package from git URL... one more time and enter: https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.uitk-navigation.git Unity resolves Graph Toolkit 0.5.0-exp.1, Input System 1.19.0, and the built-in UI Toolkit module from the package manifest. You do not need to add Graph Toolkit manually. Manifest alternative You can place the three UPM packages in Packages/manifest.json instead of using the Package Manager window: { "dependencies": { "com.annulusgames.lit-motion": "https://github.com/annulusgames/LitMotion.git?path=src/LitMotion/Assets/LitMotion", "com.cysharp.zlinq": "https://github.com/Cysharp/ZLinq.git?path=src/ZLinq.Unity/Assets/ZLinq.Unity", "com.nkstudio.uitk-navigation": "https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.uitk-navigation.git" } } The manifest entry installs ZLinq.Unity, not the core ZLinq NuGet package. Core ZLinq must still be installed with NuGetForUnity. Verify the installation After Unity finishes importing and compiling, check all of the following: Assets > Create > UI Navigation > UI Navigation Graph is available. Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog opens. LitMotion, ZLinq, ZLinq.Unity, or Graph Toolkit errors are absent from the Console. com.nkstudio.uitk-navigation appears in Package Manager. To expose the package tests in Test Runner, add "testables": ["com.nkstudio.uitk-navigation"] to the manifest.

manual/navigation-graph/application-quit.title: Application Quit node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/application-quit.summary: Application Quit node Application Quit is a terminal Action node for an exit route. It has one Enter port and no Next output. Connect a Signal, Portal, Random branch, or continuing Action chain to Enter. Runtime behavior depends on the environment: In a player build, it calls Application.Quit(). In the Unity Editor, it stops Play Mode so the route can be tested safely. The node exposes Display Name and Node Description for graph readability but has no other runtime settings. Use it behind an explicit confirmation UI or popup. On platforms where the operating system owns application lifecycle, Application.Quit() may have platform-specific behavior; keep any save or cleanup work outside this node and complete it before requesting the quit route.

manual/navigation-graph/code-first.html.title: Code-first graph authoring | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/code-first.html.summary: Code-first graph authoring UINavigationGraphBuilder is an Editor-only API for generating editable .uinavgraph assets without exposing Graph Toolkit implementation types. using NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Editor.Navigation; using NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Identity; using UnityEngine; var graph = UINavigationGraphBuilder.Create( "Assets/UI/MainNavigation.uinavgraph", overwrite: true); var start = graph.AddStart(new Vector2(40, 160)); var home = graph.AddScreen("home", "Home", new Vector2(320, 120)); var settings = graph.AddScreen("settings", "Settings", new Vector2(760, 120)) .WithHistory(useBack: true); var homePortal = graph.AddPortal( new UIKey("Global", "Home"), new Vector2(320, 420)); graph.Connect(start, home); graph.Connect(home.AddSignalOutput(new UIKey("Menu", "Settings")), settings); graph.Connect(homePortal, home); graph.Save(openGraph: true); Screen outputs can use a Database UIKey or a Custom string. Create does not touch files; Save validates, writes, imports, and optionally opens the graph. Existing assets are protected unless overwrite: true is supplied. For Send Signal/Destination authoring, create the node in Graph Toolkit and set its Database or Custom address in the Graph Inspector so it can be validated against a matching Portal.

manual/navigation-graph/debug-log.html.title: Debug Log node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/debug-log.html.summary: Debug Log node Debug Log writes a message to the Unity Console and continues to the next node. It is useful for confirming which graph branch ran without adding temporary MonoBehaviour code. Option Values Log Type Normal, Warning, Error Message Text written to the Console The Enter port must have exactly one incoming transition or continuing Action. Next is also required and must lead to one UI or Action. At runtime, Normal calls Debug.Log, Warning calls Debug.LogWarning, and Error calls Debug.LogError, using the active UINavigatorBehaviour as context. Logging does not wait or change navigation; the rest of the compiled Action chain executes immediately. Use Normal for temporary flow tracing, Warning for an unexpected but recoverable route, and Error for a route that represents an invalid application state. Remove noisy diagnostic nodes from production graphs when they are no longer useful.

manual/navigation-graph/load-scene.html.title: Load Scene node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/load-scene.html.summary: Load Scene node Load Scene starts a Unity asynchronous scene load and can optionally continue to another UI or Action. Scene settings Setting Description Reference Scene Name or Build Index Scene Name Name or path registered in Build Settings Build Index Non-negative index in Build Settings Load Mode Single or Additive Allow Scene Activation Whether the operation may activate the loaded scene Scene Activation Delay Unscaled delay after loading reaches the activation threshold The graph validates that the selected reference is non-empty or non-negative and that Activation Delay is a finite value of zero or greater. Runtime also rejects a Build Index outside SceneManager.sceneCountInBuildSettings. When Allow Scene Activation is disabled, the operation remains pending. Activate it later through the active navigator: if (UINavigatorBehaviour.Active.HasPendingSceneActivation) UINavigatorBehaviour.Active.ActivatePendingScene(); Continuation timing Next is optional for Scene Action nodes. If connected, the graph continues as soon as the load request is started; it does not wait for the scene to finish loading. Use Unity scene callbacks or application code when later work must wait for completion. With Single mode, remember that loading a new scene can destroy the current UINavigatorBehaviour unless its GameObject is preserved or the destination scene provides the next navigator.

manual/navigation-graph/pivot.html.title: Pivot node removal | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/pivot.html.summary: Pivot node removal Pivot and its rotation styler were removed in 0.4.0 to eliminate its Graph Toolkit rendering and authoring overhead. For a simple route, connect the UI output directly to the destination UI or Action. To merge outputs from A and B into one named destination, connect both outputs to the Multi Enter port of Send Signal, then configure the matching Portal to route to the actual UI. Before 0.4 0.4 replacement Pivot used only to bend a wire Direct connection Several visual paths merged at Pivot Send Signal Multi input Pivot chain ended at a UI Matching Portal output connects to that UI Important Existing graphs must remove Pivot nodes and reconnect their wires before they can be authored with 0.4.0.

manual/navigation-graph/portal.html.title: Portal node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/portal.html.summary: Portal node A Portal owns a global route. It has no Enter port and is checked before outputs on the active UI node. In 0.4.0 it is also the destination resolved by a Send Signal node. Portal Condition Setting Description Type Signal or Toggle Signal Address Database or Custom when Type is Signal Database Signal Signal catalog Category / Key Custom Signal Case-sensitive graph-local string Toggle Address Toggle catalog Category / Key Toggle Value On or Off History Push, Replace, or Back Output Required route to exactly one UI or Action chain For Send Signal routing, Address Type and value must match exactly. Database Default / Home does not match Custom Home even though their visible names are similar. Push stores the previous screen when the route reaches a UI. Replace changes UI without modifying history. Back runs connected Actions and then requests history navigation instead of entering the connected UI. Portal conditions must be unique by Type, Address Type, address, and Toggle value. Empty Custom values and invalid Database keys are rejected. Caution A matching Portal has global priority. Reusing a local Signal address in a Portal can make the active UI's own output appear unresponsive.

manual/navigation-graph/random.html.title: Random node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/random.html.summary: Random node The Random node is a transient routing screen that chooses one connected output by relative weight on the next service Tick. It does not Show or Hide a View itself. Configure outputs Add entries under Random Outputs, give each one a non-negative finite Weight, and connect it to one UI or Action chain. The percentages shown beside ports are calculated from connected outputs only. For example, connected weights 1, 1, and 2 produce approximate shares of 25%, 25%, and 50%. The absolute scale does not matter: 10, 10, and 20 produce the same result. The graph validator requires: at least one connected output; one target per connected output; every Weight to be finite and zero or greater; the sum of connected Weights to be greater than zero. Disconnected outputs show 0% and are ignored by runtime selection. Note In version 0.2.0, Random still shows inherited Node Description and Clear History fields in the Inspector, but the compiler does not copy them to the Random runtime node. In particular, Clear History has no runtime effect on Random. Runtime behavior After navigation enters Random, UINavigationService.Tick() selects a branch on the next update. If its Action chain reaches another screen, navigation uses a normal Push transition; a terminal Action branch only executes its Actions. Put Action nodes between Random and the target when the chosen branch should also change time scale, log, or manage a scene. Use Random for loot screens, rotating tips, A/B flows, or any route whose probability belongs in the graph rather than application code.

manual/navigation-graph/send-signal.html.title: Send Signal node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/send-signal.html.summary: Send Signal node The Send Signal node is a render-free destination node. It receives one or more UI outputs and routes navigation through the Portal with the same Signal address. It does not display a View and has no output port. A Signal output ─┐ ├─> Send Signal (Home) ──lookup──> Portal (Home) ──> Home UI B Time Delay ────┘ Inspector and port Field Description Display Name Optional canvas title, for example Go To Home Node Description Authoring note Clear History Clears Back and Forward history when this destination is entered Address Type Database or Custom Database Signal Signal catalog Category / Key Custom Signal Case-sensitive graph-local string Enter Multi-capacity input; accepts Signal, Time Delay, and other UI transition outputs Connect existing UI outputs directly to Enter. Do not add a special Destinations output to the UI node. When an output reaches Send Signal, the runtime resolves the matching Signal Portal and executes that Portal's History and downstream route. The graph reports an error when the address is empty, the Enter input is unconnected, or no Signal Portal has the same address type and value. Important Send Signal is terminal in the visible wire flow. Its next route belongs to the matching Portal, not to an output on the Send Signal node.

manual/navigation-graph/set-active-loade.title: Set Active Loaded Scene node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/set-active-loade.summary: Set Active Loaded Scene node Set Active Loaded Scene calls SceneManager.SetActiveScene for a scene that is already loaded. Set Scene Name to a loaded scene's name or path. This node does not load the scene. If no valid loaded scene matches, or Unity refuses to make it active, UITK Navigation writes a warning and leaves the current active scene unchanged. The Enter port requires exactly one incoming transition or continuing Action. Next can be empty to end the chain or can connect to one UI or Action. Like other Scene Actions, continuation is immediate. This node is most useful after an Additive load when newly instantiated GameObjects should belong to the added scene or when scene-local systems depend on SceneManager.GetActiveScene(). Tip Because Load Scene does not wait before following Next, do not connect Load Scene → Set Active Loaded Scene and assume the load has completed. Coordinate completion in code before requesting the route that activates the scene.

manual/navigation-graph/start.html.title: Start node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/start.html.summary: Start node The Start node selects the first screen entered when UINavigationService.Initialize() runs. Ports Port Direction Description Start Output Connects to the initial UI or Random Enter port A graph must contain exactly one Start node, and its output connects directly to exactly one screen. The default graph created from Assets > Create > UI Navigation > UI Navigation Graph already contains Start → Home. Configure Home's View commands rather than trying to assign a View directly to Start. Runtime behavior The importer compiles Start's target as the runtime asset's start screen. During initialization, the service first resynchronizes registered Views to none, then enters that screen with a Replace transition and applies its On Enter commands. Start itself is not a screen that remains active. Tip If Play Mode logs that the start node cannot be found, save the graph and fix any Start connection or validation error shown in the graph Inspector.

manual/navigation-graph/time-scale.html.title: Time Scale node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/time-scale.html.summary: Time Scale node Time Scale is a continuing Action node that assigns Time.timeScale and then follows Next. Value Typical use 0 Pause scaled gameplay 1 Restore normal time Greater than 1 Accelerate scaled gameplay The value must be finite and zero or greater. The Enter port needs exactly one incoming transition or continuing Action, and Next must connect to exactly one UI or Action. UITK Navigation ticks Time Delay outputs with Time.unscaledDeltaTime, and its LitMotion transitions use a real-time scheduler by default. UI navigation and default transitions therefore continue while Time.timeScale is 0. Tip A pause flow commonly uses UI → Time Scale (0) → Pause UI, then UI → Time Scale (1) → Game UI when resuming. Ensure every route that leaves the paused state restores the intended value.

manual/navigation-graph/ui.html.title: UI node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/ui.html.summary: UI node The UI node is the visible screen state. It applies registered View commands on enter and exit, then waits for an output to choose the next route. Inspector Option Description Display Name Canvas title Node Description Authoring note Clear History Clears Back and Forward after entering Use Back Allows this active UI to request graph Back navigation On Enter UI Animated or Instant Show/Hide commands On Exit UI Commands merged while leaving Outputs Dynamic routes originating from this UI Output types Type Matching event Signal A matching NavButton, Signal.Send(...), or Custom Signal Time Delay Unscaled seconds since this UI became active Toggle A matching NavToggle value: On, Off, or Any UI View A matching Animated Show or Hide transition starts Signal outputs select Database or Custom addressing. Database uses the Signal catalog; Custom uses an ordinal, case-sensitive graph-local string. An output connects to exactly one target. Connect directly to another UI or Action chain, or connect several UI outputs to one Send Signal Multi input. There is no Destinations output on the UI node. Duplicate Signal addresses, duplicate View conditions, and overlapping Toggle conditions such as Any plus On are validation errors. UI View outputs fire at animation start; Instant View commands do not trigger them.

manual/navigation-graph/unload-scene.htm.title: Unload Scene node | UITK Navigation
manual/navigation-graph/unload-scene.htm.summary: Unload Scene node Unload Scene requests SceneManager.UnloadSceneAsync for an already loaded scene. Set Scene Name to the scene's name or path. At runtime, UITK Navigation verifies that the scene exists and is loaded. It refuses to unload when only one scene remains and writes a warning instead, protecting the final loaded scene. The Enter port requires one incoming transition or continuing Action. Next is optional and can lead to one UI or Action. Navigation continues after the unload request is issued; it does not wait for UnloadSceneAsync to complete. Use this node for Additive content, modal gameplay scenes, or returning from a sub-scene. If later logic depends on the unload being complete, observe Unity's scene events in application code before triggering the next navigation route.

manual/requirement.html.title: Requirements | UITK Navigation
manual/requirement.html.summary: Requirements UITK Navigation targets Unity 6.6 and builds its graph authoring workflow on Unity's experimental Graph Toolkit. Item Version How it is provided Unity 6000.6.0b5 or newer Unity 6.6 is required Graph Toolkit 0.5.0-exp.1 Resolved from the UITK Navigation package manifest Input System 1.19.0 Resolved from the UITK Navigation package manifest UI Toolkit com.unity.modules.uielements 1.0.0 Built into Unity LitMotion 2.0.0 or newer Install the UPM package from Git ZLinq Compatible NuGet release plus ZLinq.Unity Install in two steps with NuGetForUnity and UPM NuGetForUnity A release compatible with Unity 6.6 Required to install the core ZLinq package ZLinq requires two packages ZLinq support in Unity is split between the core library and its Unity integration: Install the ZLinq NuGet package through Window > NuGet > Manage NuGet Packages. This menu is provided by NuGetForUnity. Install ZLinq.Unity through Unity Package Manager with this Git URL: https://github.com/Cysharp/ZLinq.git?path=src/ZLinq.Unity/Assets/ZLinq.Unity Important Installing only ZLinq.Unity is not enough. The core ZLinq assembly must also be present under Assets/Packages through NuGetForUnity. LitMotion is installed separately through Unity Package Manager: https://github.com/annulusgames/LitMotion.git?path=src/LitMotion/Assets/LitMotion The Runtime and Editor assemblies do not compile when LitMotion, core ZLinq, or ZLinq.Unity is missing. Graph Toolkit usage UITK Navigation uses Graph Toolkit internally to edit .uinavgraph files. Saving the graph runs a Scripted Importer that validates the authoring graph and compiles it into a runtime UINavigationAsset. You work in the Graph Toolkit editor, but runtime navigation reads the compiled asset. Graph Toolkit 0.5.0-exp.1 is declared by UITK Navigation and is normally installed automatically. Because it is experimental and tied to Unity 6.6 APIs, other Unity versions are not supported.

manual/uxml-elements/nav-button.html.title: NavButton | UITK Navigation
manual/uxml-elements/nav-button.html.summary: NavButton NavButton extends UI Toolkit Button. Clicking it sends its Database Signal address to the active navigator. <nav:NavButton name="open-settings" text="Settings" signal-category="Menu" signal-key="OpenSettings" /> Attribute Default Description signal-category Default Signal catalog category signal-key Empty Signal key within the category The address is exposed through the public Signal property. If it is invalid, the click logs a warning and navigation is not requested. Connect it to the graph Register Menu / OpenSettings under the Signal tab in Key Catalog. Assign it to NavButton in UI Builder. Add a Signal output to the active UI node and choose the same Database address, or use it as a Signal Portal condition. Connect the output to one UI, Action, or Send Signal target. Code can publish the same event with either Signal.Send("Menu", "OpenSettings") or Signal.Send(new UIKey("Menu", "OpenSettings")). Because NavButton inherits Button, standard attributes, USS selectors, focus behavior, and clicked remain available.

manual/uxml-elements/nav-element.html.title: NavElement | UITK Navigation
manual/uxml-elements/nav-element.html.summary: NavElement NavElement is a VisualElement that registers a View address and owns its visibility lifecycle. Navigation Graph Show/Hide commands resolve this address through the runtime UIViewRegistry. <nav:NavElement name="main" view-category="Menu" view-key="Main" hide-on-back="false" block-back="false" follow-parent="true"> <startup> <nav:UIViewStartupSettings on-start="InstantShow" hide-mode="Display" use-custom-start-position="false" auto-hide-after-show="false" auto-hide-delay="3" /> </startup> </nav:NavElement> Attributes Attribute Default Description view-category Default View catalog category view-key Empty Key within the selected category hide-on-back false Hides this visible View when it wins Back handling block-back false Consumes Back without hiding this View follow-parent true Follows the visibility of an enclosing NavElement Category and Key must both contain text. Comparison is ordinal and case-sensitive. The View registers only while attached to a Player-context panel and unregisters when detached. Startup settings On Start Initial behavior Disabled Uses the current resolved display state Instant Hide Starts hidden without animation Instant Show Starts visible without animation Animation Hide Starts visible and plays Hide Animation Show Starts hidden and plays Show The nested UIViewStartupSettings object accepts these attributes: Attribute Default Description on-start Disabled Initial behavior from the table above hide-mode Display Whether a hidden View leaves layout use-custom-start-position true Applies a pixel start translation before Move is prepared custom-start-position (0, 0, 0) Translation used when the custom start position is enabled auto-hide-after-show false Schedules Hide after Show finishes auto-hide-delay 3 Unscaled seconds before Auto Hide When Hidden selects Display (display: none, removed from layout) or Visibility (visibility: hidden, layout preserved). A Custom Start Position applies a pixel translate before Move values are prepared. Auto Hide after Show starts an unscaled timer only after Show finishes. See Transition animation for Show/Hide presets and manual channels. Nested Views and Back A nested NavElement with follow-parent="true" shows and hides with its nearest parent View. The parent waits for following children to settle before reporting completion. Set it to false when the child represents an independent overlay. hide-on-back and block-back participate before graph history. Enable only the behavior you intend; a visible View that consumes Back can prevent the active UI node's Use Back route. Runtime API NavElement view = root.Q<NavElement>("main"); view.Show(); // configured Show transition view.Hide(); // configured Hide transition view.InstantShow(); view.InstantHide(); Debug.Log($"{view.Id}: {view.IsVisible}"); Visibility exposes the underlying UIViewVisibility for state events, scheduler selection, and direct Show/Hide UIAnimation settings. RestoreStartState() reapplies the configured startup state, and InvalidateAnimationStartValues() recaptures Move references after layout changes. If multiple NavElement instances register the same UIKey, a graph command intentionally fans out to all of them. Use distinct View keys when the instances must move independently.

manual/uxml-elements/nav-toggle.html.title: NavToggle | UITK Navigation
manual/uxml-elements/nav-toggle.html.summary: NavToggle NavToggle extends UI Toolkit Toggle. Whenever its value changes, it publishes a Toggle address together with the new bool value. <nav:NavToggle name="music" label="Music" value="true" toggle-category="Settings" toggle-key="Music" /> Attribute Default Description toggle-category Default Toggle catalog category toggle-key Empty Toggle key within the category The public Toggle property returns the combined UIKey. An empty Category or Key logs a [NavToggle] warning when the value changes and does not send an event. Connect it to the graph Register the address under Key Catalog's Button tab. There is no separate Toggle catalog. Assign it to NavToggle in UI Builder. Choose + Add Output > UIToggle to create one or more Toggle ports on the active UI node. Select the same address and choose a condition: Condition Matches On true only Off false only Any Either value Do not combine Any with On or Off for the same address, and do not repeat a condition; the graph compiler treats overlapping routes as an error. Application code can publish the same event with: UINavigationEvents.RequestToggle("Settings", "Music", enabled); NavToggle keeps the standard Toggle API, binding behavior, and USS styling. The package adds the ui-navigation-toggle USS class.
